name: Tillett Textiles
old_description: Before clients like Billy Baldwin, Albert Hadley, Babe Paley, and Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis discovered Tillett, the British-born Tillett brothers were printing fabrics in Cuernavaca, where their work caught the attention of the legendary Alexey Brodovitch at Harper's Bazaar. He sent d.d. Tillett to profile the brothers, and she soon fell in love with Leslie Tillett. Together they founded Tillett in 1946 and moved to the Upper East Side, living above their brownstone boutique and custom screen-printing atelier. There, the pair pioneered techniques such as drag box, wax resist, layering, and transparent inks to create painterly hand-printed fabrics prized by stylish clients.
about:
Tillett Textiles was founded in 1946 on Manhattan's Upper East Side by d.d. Tillett, a Harper's Bazaar writer, and Leslie Tillett, one of the British-born brothers who had been hand-printing fabrics in Cuernavaca, Mexico. The pair lived above their brownstone boutique and custom screen-printing atelier, where they pioneered techniques such as drag box printing, wax resist, layering, and transparent inks to create painterly hand-printed textiles.

Today the company operates a studio in New Jersey where textiles are still produced entirely by hand using the same methods. Artisans mix custom pigment-based inks and print on linens, cottons, blends, and silks using silk screens — many dating to the 1960s — and drag boxes, a Tillett innovation. The offering spans a readily available collection sold through F. Schumacher & Co. and a bespoke service that allows clients to customize colorways, patterns, grounds, and stripe sizes from the historic archive.

The brand has served interior designers and tastemakers since the mid‑20th century, counting Billy Baldwin, Albert Hadley, Babe Paley, Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, Bunny Mellon, and Diana Vreeland among its clients. Tillett fabrics have been used in the White House, the Oak Spring Estate, and are held in the collections of the Museum of Modern Art, the Philadelphia Museum of Art, and the Cooper Hewitt Smithsonian Design Museum.

The company's stated distinction lies in its philosophy rooted in nature, imperfection, and the artistry of the handmade. As the firm describes it, only the hand can moderate the dialogue between fabric and ink, and customization down to the tiniest detail remains its calling card.

name: Titan Circuits
old_description: Titan Circuits — a division of Outroar LLC — specializes in high-mix, low to medium volume electronic manufacturing services in the USA. We operate on the principal that quality is built into all of our processes. From beginning to end, quality is in the forefront. We are committed to providing cost-effective, high-quality PCB assembly services with superior customer service.
about:
Titan Circuits operates from Phoenix, Arizona, as a division of Outroar LLC. The company specializes in high-mix, low- to medium-volume electronic manufacturing services, focusing on printed circuit board assembly for customers across the United States and abroad.

Its core offering is PCB assembly, covering surface-mount technology down to 01005 passives, QFNs, BGAs, and micro-BGAs, through-hole and selective soldering, flexible and rigid-flex circuit assembly, box-build integration, cable and wire harness fabrication, and functional testing. The shop handles prototype runs through low- to medium-volume production, providing turnkey, consigned, and partially kitted supply-chain options.

The customer base spans military and defense (ITAR and SAM registered), aerospace (AS9100D certified, serving aerospace firms), medical (RoHS IPC Class 3 devices), automotive (power and RF boards for autonomous vehicles), industrial (control systems for harsh environments), and telecommunications (RF assemblies including Rogers/FR4 hybrids). Clients range from small startups to large global enterprises.

Titan Circuits emphasizes built-in quality, with staff certified to IPC-A-610G and IPC J-STD-001G with the Space Addendum, and a full-time IPC trainer on site. Recent equipment investments include a DEK Horizon Neo iX printer, dual-gantry Yamaha YSM20-2 pick-and-place machines, a BTU reflow oven, Koh Young Zenith 2 3D AOI, an Assure X-ray component counter, Nordson selective solder, and an Aqueous Zero Ion ionic contamination tester.

old_description: Topper Town solves these problems with proven, practical solutions. Serving Albuquerque, NM since 1983, this family owned business brings decades of hands on experience. Every recommendation comes from real world use, not guesswork or pressure tactics.
about:
Topper Town has operated from Albuquerque, New Mexico since 1983 as a family-owned business. The company began serving local truck owners with accessories and installation services, building a reputation over four decades of hands-on experience in the region.

The shop supplies and professionally installs a range of truck accessories including camper shells, tonneau covers, bed liners, toolboxes, and racks. Each product is selected for durability, safety, and ease of use, and the installation work focuses on proper sealing and long-term performance. The facility on Osuna Road NE serves as both a showroom and installation bay.

Customers include individual truck owners and commercial fleets across the Albuquerque area who need weather protection, cargo security, and organized storage. The team advises on product choices based on work demands, travel habits, and local climate conditions such as intense sun, dust, and sudden weather changes.

The company emphasizes honest guidance without pressure tactics, drawing recommendations from real-world use rather than guesswork. Local knowledge of Albuquerque roads and weather informs every sale and installation, and many customers return years later for upgrades or refer coworkers and family.

name: Tops Packaging Solutions
old_description: To become the leading provider of innovative, sustainable, and high-quality packaging solutions across the United States. We aim to set new standards in the industry by delivering excellence in service, building lasting partnerships, and empowering businesses with reliable, eco-friendly packaging that makes a difference.
about:
Tops Packaging Solutions operates from Dowelltown, Tennessee, as a wholly-owned U.S. wholesale disposable packaging company. The business began with a focus on plastic food packaging and has accumulated over ten years of experience serving supermarkets and global retail brands.

The company manufactures a range of foodservice packaging including cold drink cups, coffee cups, clamshell containers, meat trays, spoons, and plates. Production takes place in a 10,000-square-meter dust-free workshop equipped with automatic production lines, supported by a workforce of 175 employees, five senior managers, and a fleet of more than 80 delivery vehicles. The company states it can fulfill orders ranging from 1,000 to one million units.

Customers include supermarkets, global retail chains, restaurants, food trucks, catering operations, and event planners. The company highlights its work with supermarkets and global retail brands, and its products are used for meal prep, takeout, catering, parties, weddings, and outdoor activities.

Tops Packaging Solutions emphasizes customization services with confidentiality, a one-stop service model backed by over a decade of industry experience, and an in-house logistics department that manages delivery planning and customs clearance. All food-contact products are certified compliant with U.S. FDA guidelines, and the company pledges to replace any product that does not meet standards.

name: Toshiba International Corporation
old_description: Toshiba International Corporation manufactures a wide range of electrical equipment, including low- and medium-voltage switchgear, motors, drives and controllers. Switchgear products are used in power distribution and control applications.
about:
Toshiba International Corporation (TIC) was established in 1975 in Houston, Texas, as the U.S. manufacturing subsidiary of Japan's Toshiba Corporation. The company operates from its Houston headquarters with a workforce of 500 to 999 employees.

TIC manufactures low- and medium-voltage motors, switchgear, drives, and controllers. Its product portfolio also includes high-performance motors for extreme-duty applications, hybrid vehicle systems, and power electronics such as uninterruptible power supply (UPS) units and solar inverters. The facility supports production across these lines, though specific floor space and annual volumes are not disclosed.

The company serves the power generation, industrial, and energy sectors, with motors and drives deployed in oil and gas operations, general manufacturing, water treatment plants, and sustainable transportation projects. Its UPS and energy storage solutions provide backup power for data centers, healthcare facilities, and other mission-critical installations. Hybrid vehicle systems support automotive original equipment manufacturers.

TIC emphasizes innovation and reliability, positioning its technologies as enabling a resilient future through efficiency gains in motor performance, hybrid propulsion, and power electronics. The division was created to deliver manufacturing and infrastructure solutions that complement Toshiba's broader energy and electronics portfolio in the Americas.

name: Traco Packaging - A Division of Traco Manufacturing, Inc.
old_description: Traco packaging professionals can assist you with the right shrink film and labels to meet all of your company’s packaging challenges. Trusted by the most iconic brands as well as new start-ups and private label brands. You too can trust Traco, your shrink-sleeve label manufacturer.
about:
Traco Packaging, a division of Traco Manufacturing, Inc., has operated from Orem, Utah since its founding in 1985. The company began as a packaging specialist focused on shrink-sleeve labels and has expanded its capabilities over nearly four decades.

Today Traco produces a range of packaging products including shrink sleeves, pressure-sensitive labels, stand-up pouches, three-side-seal pouches, roll stock, PVC shrink bands, shrink bags, and multi-pack bundling. Production runs on a mix of flexographic and digital presses: a Uteco Onyx XS 36-inch flexographic press, several HP Indigo digital presses (200K, 25K, 6600, 6900), a Gidue Master M5 630 9K 26-inch press, and a Nilpeter FA Line 17-inch flexographic press. The company also supplies label applicators and packaging equipment to help customers fill, pack, and ship.

Traco serves brand owners across the consumer packaged goods spectrum, from established national brands to start-ups and private-label companies. Its customers use the packaging for products that require high-quality graphics, tamper evidence, and shelf appeal.

The company emphasizes its equipment depth and experienced team as a way to deliver consistent print quality without delays. It highlights fast turnaround on short runs, variable data and security ink capabilities, and the ability to handle both long and short production runs on the same platform.

name: Traditional Woodworks
old_description: Traditional Woodworks was founded in 1986 by Michael Pouliotte, a craftsman with a background in boatbuilding—an industry where precision, durability, and problem-solving are essential. That foundation laid the groundwork for a woodworking company built on a deep respect for traditional techniques.
about:
Traditional Woodworks operates from Berwick, Maine, where it was founded in 1986 by Michael Pouliotte, a craftsman whose background in boatbuilding instilled a focus on precision and durability. The company remains privately held and is now led by president Brooks Hausser, a fellow boatbuilding veteran with a BFA in architecture and building science.

The shop produces custom architectural millwork, including moldings, paneling, custom doors and window casings, staircases and railings, furniture, cabinetry, and marine carpentry such as teak decks and yacht interiors. Work is executed through a blend of traditional joinery and modern project management, though the company does not disclose facility size, headcount, or annual volume.

Customers include homeowners, architects, and builders seeking historic restoration or high-end residential millwork, as well as marine clients requiring fine wood components for yachts and wooden boats. Projects referenced on the company's site range from the Tower House and Timber Lake House to summer homes and marine installations.

The firm traces its differentiation to its boatbuilding roots, emphasizing problem-solving, integrity, and a respect for traditional techniques that are adapted to contemporary design needs.

about:
Tri-Fab Steel, Inc. was founded in 1971 in Birmingham, Alabama. The company began with approximately 8,000 square feet of manufacturing space and has since expanded to over 80,000 square feet.

The shop specializes in heavy industrial fabrication using carbon steel and stainless steel. Its capabilities include structural steel fabrication, as well as bins, ducts, and hoppers. Tri-Fab works from customer design drawings to produce shop details, erection prints, and all necessary hardware for complete installations. Projects typically range from a few tons up to 150 tons. The facility is equipped with overhead cranes in every bay and a Hyd-Mech 16-inch CNC band saw with power feed, among other fabrication equipment.

Tri-Fab serves a variety of industrial customers, though specific sectors are not detailed in its public materials. The company describes its clientele as an array of different types, focusing on heavy industrial applications.

Tri-Fab emphasizes that its well-equipped shop, combined with experienced personnel, enables it to meet most fabrication requirements. The business was built to provide complete installation packages from design through hardware supply.

name: Tri-Steel Manufacturing Co
old_description: Tristeel Manufacturing Co., a manufacturer and industrial supplier, was founded in 1962 by Adolph (Toby) Tobiason, Milton Homstad, and Louis Peabody. Its principle business was manufacturing and repairing of machinery for the local potato and agricultural industries in the Red River Valley of North Dakota and Minnesota.
about:
Tri-Steel Manufacturing Co. was founded in 1962 in Grand Forks, North Dakota, by Adolph (Toby) Tobiason, Milton Homstad, and Louis Peabody. The company began by manufacturing and repairing machinery for the potato and agricultural industries in the Red River Valley spanning North Dakota and Minnesota.

Today, Tri-Steel operates as a full-service manufacturer with capabilities spanning administration, marketing, engineering, procurement, and production. Its primary business is the design and manufacture of potato equipment, including Logan Potato Equipment, and complete processing lines that move produce from field to final consumer packaging. The company also produces individual parts and finished equipment for supply chains in wind energy, power generation, grain handling, and general contract manufacturing. A full-service machine shop and a large steel inventory support both production and retail sales, while an MRO division distributes replacement parts from brands such as Browning, TECO Westinghouse, Rexnord, Morse, Carlisle, Timken, and Lovejoy.

Tri-Steel serves the potato and agricultural sectors across the Red River Valley, as well as customers in wind energy, power generation, and grain handling. Its contract manufacturing work extends to diverse industrial supply chains, and its MRO distribution supports local and regional maintenance operations.

The company emphasizes its integrated approach, combining design, engineering, procurement, and manufacturing under one roof to deliver complete equipment solutions and rapid parts availability.
